reason: the correctness lens's findings the code or a test must fix

findings.text: correctness lens, high: DSCMBR-1 skip guard uses `stage_statuses[$s] == "complete"` but that field is not reset between iterations, so a member that was complete in iter k-1 and was never reached in iter k (because SIGINT fired at the per-stage abort check before dispatch) still has status "complete" and is incorrectly skipped on resume into iter k. (core/pipeline/cycle-orchestrator.sh:1468; fix: code)

correctness lens, medium: DSCMBR-1 test hand-crafts `stage_statuses.test = "in_progress"`, a value `_cycle_state_write_member_atomic` never writes to `stage_statuses`; the real status when a stage is interrupted mid-execution is "aborted", and when it was never reached is "complete" from a prior iter — using an impossible value means the skip-guard check (`== "complete"`) is never actually tested for the production data shape. (tests/integration/resume-loop-state-test.sh:272; fix: test)

correctness lens, medium: Path-traversal guard for the auto-resume `latest` symlink uses `${_lr_original_state_dir%%/}` to strip a trailing slash before constructing the prefix pattern, but `%%/` only strips a single trailing `/`; a state_dir with two trailing slashes produces a pattern with one embedded slash that will reject legitimate per-run subdirectories, silently falling back to a fresh start rather than resuming. (core/pipeline/runner.sh:2256; fix: code)
